q: He was delighted to hear some music and listened with emotion to the wild qasidas that the old man sang – songs of the Arab canon full of the wild heart-sickness of the desert.
The qasida is a formal multithematic ode addressed to a member of the elite in praise.
2000, María Rosa Menocal, Raymond P. Scheindlin, The Literature of Al-Andalus:

e: Arabic قَصْر (qaṣr), from Latin castrum; Doublet of castrum and ksar.
q: Two ruined Qasrs stand sentinel over the eastern approach to the oasis; behind them are three small patches of Ithil trees, between which and the village stand a dozen walled palm-groves […]
